title: Use of Tracer Dyes to Label Neural Projections to Lower Urinary Tract Organs
author: Janet R Keast
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.w3dfgi6
materials: Prepare tracer dye solutions: Fluorogold or Fast Blue (each 2% w/v in sterile water).
Shave and clean the ventral abdomen.

steps.title: Anesthetize and Prepare Animal
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal and prepare for surgery.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize animal using 2.5% isoflurane in oxygen, or as required for maintenance.
Place animal on a heated pad.

steps.title: Expose Injection Site
steps.instruction: Perform a midline incision in the skin and then the muscle, then gently move organs to visualize the required injection site.

steps.title: Microinject Tracer Solution
steps.instruction: Microinject sterile tracer solution at the selected injection site using a Hamilton Neuros Syringe attached to a 33G needle.

substeps.instruction: Hold the needle in place for ~5 seconds after ejection of the dye to enable spread to underlying tissue and minimize leakage.
For bladder body (dome) injections: inject bilaterally on dorsal and ventral aspects (total volume ~5 µl).
For bladder trigone or dorsal aspect of the proximal urethra: perform single injections (maximum 0.3 µl per injection).

steps.title: Clean and Close Incision
steps.instruction: Clean the injection sites and close the surgical opening.

substeps.instruction: Wash all injection sites with sterile saline.
Close the muscle and skin using approved procedures.

steps.title: Postoperative Care
steps.instruction: Administer analgesics and monitor the animal during the postoperative period as per local approved procedure.

steps.title: Tissue Fixation and Collection
steps.instruction: Fix the animals and collect tissues 5-14 days after surgery to analyze tracer dye distribution.

substeps.instruction: Remove tissues of interest, typically including dorsal root ganglia (DRG) from L1, L2, L6 and S1 spinal levels and the pelvic ganglia (major pelvic ganglia).
Remove lower urinary tract tissues for microscopic validation of the tracer injection site.
